exposure: transplacental passage of maternal antibodies (SSA/Ro, SSB/La or U1 ribonucleoproteins)
cohort: The study describes twin newborns delivered at 38 weeks gestation, who both presented with complete congenital heart block due to neonatal lupus erythematosus, with both twins and their mother testing positive for antinuclear, anti-SSA, and anti-SSB antibodies.
finding: This case report demonstrates that neonatal lupus erythematosus can cause complete congenital heart block in twins, necessitating pacemaker implantation, and that such intervention can lead to a favorable immediate and long-term evolution.
mod_finding: The newborns were delivered by caesarean section.
